youtube.title: How to Follow Up on a Quote: One Text for Plumbing, HVAC and Electrical Owners
youtube.description:
How to follow up on a quote that went quiet.
For plumbing, HVAC, electrical and home service business owners.
ServiceTitan's own data shows only 37% of estimates close on the first visit, which leaves most jobs riding on follow-up ("Follow-Ups 101: Back 2 Basics," ServiceTitan blog, 2026). Jobber's quote follow-up tips: use the client's name and the job details, and ask a question. Text it, don't email it: ServiceTitan's follow-up webinar notes that texts outperform email on open rates, and in a Housecall Pro survey of 1,040 U.S. homeowners (2025), 59% said they expect text updates.

The text:
Hi [name], it's [you]. Still want that water heater swapped before winter?

When to send it (Jobber Academy, quote follow-up templates):
1. Within 2 days of the quote.
2. A week after the quote.
3. 1 to 2 days before it expires.
After 3 with no reply, close the file.

One name, one job, one question. Send this to whoever follows up on your quotes.
The Text, lesson 2. Previous lesson: how to respond to leads fast.
Next lesson: why your markup is not your profit.
